title: Risk Assessment: Sync pipeline state branch to remote for durability
summary: Assessment of the architect's recommended approach: push-at-phase-boundaries for the `egg/pipeline-state` branch (Option C) combined with pre-validation data sanitization for schema drift (Option I). The approach is sound and low-complexity compared to alternatives. However, code review uncovered a critical implementation blocker: the gateway's `validate_repo_path()` restricts git operations to paths under `/home/egg/repos/` and `/home/egg/.egg-worktrees/`, but the state worktree lives at `/home/egg/.egg-state/pipeline-worktree` — outside all allowed paths. A naive push from the state worktree will be rejected with 403. This must be addressed in implementation. Five risks are rated Medium, three Low, and one is rated High (the path validation blocker). All are mitigable with the proposed strategies.

risk_assessment.overall_verdict: Proceed with the architect's recommended approach (Option C + Option I). The implementation is well-scoped (6 files, 2 work areas) and builds on proven patterns (existing GatewayClient push/fetch). The highest risk is the gateway path validation blocker (R-1), which requires either adding the state worktree path to ALLOWED_REPO_PATHS or pushing from the main repo path. All other risks are manageable with the proposed mitigations.
risk_assessment.confidence: High — based on source code analysis of state_store.py, gateway_client.py, gateway.py, git_client.py, policy.py, startup_reconciliation.py, cli.py, and routes/pipelines.py

risks.title: Gateway path validation rejects state worktree path
risks.description: The gateway's `validate_repo_path()` in git_client.py:202-228 only allows git operations from paths under ALLOWED_REPO_PATHS: `/home/egg/repos/`, `/home/egg/.egg-worktrees/`, and `/repos/`. The state worktree lives at `/home/egg/.egg-state/pipeline-worktree`, which is outside all allowed paths. A push from this path will be rejected with 403 by the gateway before any branch ownership or file restriction checks run. The architect's plan proposes reusing `push_worktree_branch()` with the state worktree path, but this will fail at the path validation layer.

mitigation.strategy: Push from the main repo path instead of the state worktree path, OR add the state path to ALLOWED_REPO_PATHS
steps: Option A (preferred): Push the state branch from the main repo path (`/home/egg/repos/{repo}`). Since `egg/pipeline-state` is a local branch in the main repo, `git push origin egg/pipeline-state` works from the main repo directory. The push_state_branch() method should use `self.repo_path` (main repo) as the repo_path argument, not `self._worktree_dir`. The refspec should be `egg/pipeline-state:egg/pipeline-state`.

Option B (alternative): Add `/home/egg/.egg-state/` to ALLOWED_REPO_PATHS in gateway/git_client.py. This is simpler but broadens the gateway's trust boundary to include the state volume, which may have security implications.
Option A is preferred because it avoids expanding the gateway's allowed paths and uses the existing infrastructure correctly.
mitigation.human_review_reason: The choice between expanding ALLOWED_REPO_PATHS vs. pushing from the main repo affects the gateway's security boundary. Human should confirm the approach.

risks.title: Startup fetch overwrites unpushed local state changes
risks.description: The architect proposes 'remote wins' semantics on startup: `git fetch` + `git reset --hard origin/egg/pipeline-state`. If the orchestrator crashes mid-phase (between phase-boundary pushes) and restarts, any state changes since the last push are lost. This includes: agent heartbeat updates, container status transitions, decision resolutions, and intermediate pipeline status changes. While the architect correctly notes this represents 'at most one phase boundary of drift', the lost state could include decision resolutions (HITL responses) that a human already submitted, causing them to be re-requested.

mitigation.strategy: Prefer local state when it exists; only use remote as fallback for empty/missing local state
steps: On startup, check if the local state branch has commits. If it does, local state is authoritative — skip the remote fetch or merge rather than overwrite.
Only use `git reset --hard origin/egg/pipeline-state` when the local branch is empty or doesn't exist (fresh volume/new host scenario).
If a merge approach is too complex, at minimum compare local and remote HEAD timestamps or commit counts before deciding which wins.
The simple heuristic: if local worktree has pipeline files, trust local. If local worktree is empty or missing, fetch from remote.

risks.title: Temporary session ID collision between worktree and state branch pushes
risks.description: The existing `push_worktree_branch()` creates temp sessions with container_id `{pipeline_id}-failsafe-push`. If the new `push_state_branch()` also creates temp sessions at the same phase-boundary call sites, it needs a distinct container_id. If both use the same container_id pattern and execute concurrently (or if the first session cleanup fails), the second registration will either fail or reuse a stale session.

mitigation.strategy: Use a distinct container_id pattern for state branch push sessions
steps: Use `{pipeline_id}-state-push` or `state-branch-push` as the temp container_id for state branch push operations.
Ensure the session cleanup in the finally block completes before the next push attempt.
Consider serializing the two pushes (worktree branch first, state branch second) rather than running them concurrently.

risks.title: Startup latency from remote fetch blocks request serving
risks.description: The architect proposes calling `fetch_state_branch()` at startup before health check initialization (cli.py:132-145). If the gateway is slow to respond or the remote fetch is large (many pipeline state files accumulated over time), this blocks the orchestrator from serving requests. The current startup sequence already includes reconciliation and health checks — adding a network round-trip to the gateway compounds startup latency.

mitigation.strategy: Make startup fetch non-blocking with a timeout
steps: Set a short timeout (e.g., 10 seconds) on the startup fetch. If it times out, continue with local state.
Alternatively, run the fetch in a background thread after the server starts accepting requests, and flag state as 'sync pending' until complete.
Ensure the fetch is truly best-effort: if the gateway isn't healthy yet (common during container orchestration where services start in parallel), skip the fetch gracefully.

risks.title: Pipeline state data exposed to remote repository
risks.description: Pipeline state files contain operational metadata: container IDs, IP addresses (127.0.0.1 for temp sessions), error messages with stack traces, agent execution history, and HITL decision content. Pushing to remote makes this visible to anyone with repository read access. While this is a private repository, it changes the data exposure surface from 'Docker volume on one host' to 'anyone with repo access'.

mitigation.strategy: Accept the risk — data is operational, not secret
steps: Pipeline state files don't contain secrets (tokens, credentials, API keys). The gateway holds credentials separately.
Container IDs and internal IPs (127.0.0.1) are transient and not exploitable.
Error messages may contain stack traces but these are already visible in logs.
This matches the precedent set by `egg/checkpoints/v2` which already pushes similar operational data to remote.
Document in PR description that pipeline state pushed to remote contains operational metadata only.

risks.title: Sanitization function requires ongoing maintenance as enums evolve
risks.description: The proposed `sanitize_pipeline_data()` function must maintain sets of valid enum values at module level. When new enum values are added or removed from models.py, the sanitization function must be updated in lockstep. If a developer adds a new enum to the Pipeline model (e.g., a new field with enum values) but doesn't add sanitization logic for it, old state files with unknown values for that field will still fail validation.

mitigation.strategy: Build valid enum sets dynamically from the model enums rather than hardcoding
steps: Use `{v.value for v in AgentRole}` to build the valid set at module load time, not a hardcoded list.
Write the sanitization to walk the model schema (via Pydantic's model_json_schema() or field annotations) to discover which fields are enums, rather than hardcoding field names.
Add a unit test that validates the sanitization function handles all current enum fields — this test will fail if a new enum field is added without sanitization coverage.

Alternatively, use a simpler approach: catch ValidationError on load, parse the error details to identify the offending field/value, and apply targeted fixes. This is more reactive but requires zero maintenance.

risks.title: State branch push serialization with pipeline state locking
risks.description: The state store uses both `fcntl.flock` (cross-process) and `threading.RLock` (in-process) for serializing git operations in the state worktree. The proposed push operation needs to interact correctly with this locking: if push acquires the lock, it blocks all state saves during the network round-trip; if push runs outside the lock, it risks pushing a partial state (e.g., mid-write of a JSON file). Since pushes go through the gateway API (not local git), they're already decoupled from the worktree's git index — but the gateway push handler will run `git diff` against the branch to check changed files (if session_role is set).

mitigation.strategy: Push outside the state store lock since the gateway operates on git refs, not the working tree
steps: The push operation sends a refspec to the gateway, which pushes the committed state. It doesn't read the working tree directly.
Since temp sessions have no session_role, the gateway skips file restriction checks (line 652 condition) and won't call get_changed_files_in_push(). No git diff runs against the state worktree.
The push should NOT hold the _git_op lock. It operates on committed refs and the gateway handles its own git operations.
Ensure push_state_branch() is called after _commit_state() completes and the lock is released.

risks.title: Dropped agent executions may affect pipeline status display and reporting
risks.description: The sanitization drops agent executions with unknown roles (e.g., `reviewer_unified`). These pipelines are likely terminal (old, completed/failed), but if users or dashboards enumerate agent executions to show pipeline history, the dropped agents will be invisible. The pipeline's overall status and phase history remain intact, but per-agent reporting will have gaps.

mitigation.strategy: Log sanitized changes and preserve original data in a metadata field
steps: Log at WARNING level when agents are dropped, including the pipeline ID, dropped role value, and agent count.
Optionally add a `_sanitized_agents` field to the sanitized data that preserves the raw dicts of dropped agents for debugging. Pydantic's extra='allow' or a dedicated field could hold this.
The auto-migration re-save (sanitized data written back to disk) should be opt-in, not automatic. This preserves the original JSON for forensics.

risks.title: All pipelines' state pushed atomically on every phase boundary
risks.description: The `egg/pipeline-state` branch contains state files for ALL pipelines (active and terminal). A single `git push origin egg/pipeline-state` pushes the entire branch — all pipeline state files. Over time, as pipelines accumulate (no cleanup mechanism exists), the branch grows. Each push transfers the entire ref difference, which grows with the number of pipeline state commits. This is bounded by git's delta compression but could become noticeable at scale.
affected_files: orchestrator/state_store.py:40 (STATE_BRANCH — single branch for all pipelines)

mitigation.strategy: Accept for now; consider periodic gc or archival later
steps: Git push only transfers new commits since the last push, not the entire branch history. This bounds the per-push transfer size to the changes since the last push.
Terminal pipeline state files are small (~5-20KB JSON each). Even with hundreds of pipelines, the total is manageable.
A separate cleanup issue (out of scope per architect) can address archival of terminal pipelines.
Monitor push latency in logs to detect if this becomes a problem.

remote_sync_option_c.verdict: Agree — phase-boundary pushing is the right tradeoff
remote_sync_option_c.notes: The 8-12 pushes per lifecycle is well within acceptable overhead. The choice to avoid per-commit pushing (Option A) is correct — pipeline state changes far too frequently. Background sync (Option B) adds unnecessary complexity.

schema_sanitization_option_i.verdict: Agree — pre-validation sanitization is cleaner than model validators
schema_sanitization_option_i.notes: The approach of building valid enum sets from the actual Python enums (rather than hardcoding) would make it more maintainable. The decision to drop unknown agents rather than mapping them is correct — semantic accuracy of historical data matters less than loadability.

gaps_identified.gap: Gateway path validation not addressed in implementation plan
gaps_identified.details: The implementation plan assumes push_worktree_branch/fetch_worktree_branch can be reused with the state worktree path. The state worktree at `/home/egg/.egg-state/pipeline-worktree` is outside ALLOWED_REPO_PATHS in gateway/git_client.py:162-166. The implementation must either push from the main repo path (preferred) or expand ALLOWED_REPO_PATHS.

gaps_identified.gap: Startup fetch ordering with respect to gateway readiness
gaps_identified.details: The plan inserts the fetch call between startup reconciliation and health check init (cli.py). But during container orchestration, the gateway sidecar may not be ready yet when the orchestrator starts. The plan doesn't address this dependency ordering or specify a timeout/retry strategy.

gaps_identified.gap: Fetch-on-startup 'remote wins' semantics are too aggressive
gaps_identified.details: The plan specifies `git reset --hard origin/egg/pipeline-state` on startup. This overwrites any local state that wasn't pushed (e.g., from a crash between phase boundaries). A safer approach: only reset if local state is empty/missing; prefer local when it has content.

gaps_identified.gap: No consideration of temp session container_id uniqueness for state push
gaps_identified.details: The existing push_worktree_branch uses `{pipeline_id}-failsafe-push` as the temp container_id. The new state branch push needs its own distinct ID pattern to avoid session collisions.

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: If Option B (adding `/home/egg/.egg-state/` to ALLOWED_REPO_PATHS) is chosen for R-1, this broadens the gateway's trust boundary. Human should confirm this is acceptable or prefer Option A (push from main repo path).
The choice between 'remote always wins' and 'local preferred, remote as fallback' affects data loss behavior during crash recovery. Human should confirm the desired semantics.

rollback_plan.description: Both work areas (remote sync and schema sanitization) are independently revertable.
steps: Remote sync: Remove the push_state_branch/fetch_state_branch calls from phase boundary call sites and cli.py startup. The state branch continues to work locally-only as before. No data migration needed — the remote copy of the branch is harmless.
Schema sanitization: Revert the sanitize_pipeline_data call in load_pipeline(). Old pipelines with unknown enums will resume causing validation errors on startup — same as current behavior.
If the remote state branch has been pushed and later needs to be removed, `git push origin --delete egg/pipeline-state` cleans it up. This does not affect local state.

test_strategy_review.architect_coverage: The architect's test strategy covers the key unit and integration scenarios. The proposed tests are appropriate.
additional_tests_recommended: Unit test: push_state_branch uses main repo path (not worktree path) as repo_path argument, validating R-1 mitigation
Unit test: sanitize_pipeline_data builds valid enum sets dynamically from model enums (not hardcoded), validating R-6 mitigation
Integration test: startup fetch when gateway is unavailable completes within timeout and doesn't block startup (R-4 mitigation)
Unit test: temp session container_id for state push is distinct from worktree push container_id (R-3 mitigation)
Regression test: load_pipeline still raises StateValidationError for genuinely corrupt JSON (not just schema drift), ensuring sanitization doesn't mask real corruption
